title: Ligaments and menisci of the knee (posterior)
attribution: 3D anatomy from Z-Anatomy, built on BodyParts3D (CC BY-SA). Rendered in Blender; surface detail added with an image model.

rows: Attachments
Posterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the lateral surface of the medial condyle of the femur.
Function
Stops the tibia from sliding backward on the femur. It is the main stabilizer of the flexed, weight-bearing knee, as in walking downhill.
hy: Torn by a blow to the front of the tibia with the knee bent (dashboard injury). The posterior drawer test is positive.

rows: Attachments
Anterior intercondylar area of the tibia to the medial surface of the lateral condyle of the femur.
Function
Stops the tibia from sliding forward on the femur and limits hyperextension of the knee.
hy: Torn in twisting and sudden-stop injuries. The anterior drawer and Lachman tests are positive. The unhappy triad is an injury to this ligament, the tibial collateral ligament and a meniscus.

rows: Location
C-shaped plate of fibrocartilage on the medial condyle of the tibia.
Function
Deepens the surface of the tibia, spreads the load and absorbs shock.
hy: It is attached to the tibial collateral ligament, so it moves less than the lateral meniscus and is torn along with that ligament.
McMurray test for a medial tear: pain or a click as the knee is extended with the leg rotated externally.

rows: Location
Nearly circular plate of fibrocartilage on the lateral condyle of the tibia. It is not attached to the fibular collateral ligament.
Function
Deepens the surface of the tibia, spreads the load and absorbs shock.
hy: McMurray test for a lateral tear: pain or a click as the knee is extended with the leg rotated internally.

structures.name: Tibial (medial) collateral ligament
objects: Superficial part of tibial collateral ligament.r
Deep part of tibial collateral ligament.r

rows: Attachments
Medial epicondyle of the femur to the medial condyle and upper medial surface of the tibia. Its deep fibers are attached to the medial meniscus.
Function
Resists forces that push the knee inward (valgus stress).
hy: Injured by a blow to the lateral side of the knee. The leg can then be abducted abnormally at the knee (positive valgus stress test). It is part of the unhappy triad with the anterior cruciate ligament and a meniscus.

rows: Attachments
Lateral epicondyle of the femur to the head of the fibula. It is a round cord, separate from the joint capsule and the lateral meniscus.
Function
Resists forces that push the knee outward (varus stress).
hy: When it is torn the leg can be adducted abnormally at the knee (positive varus stress test).

rows: Attachments
Tendon of popliteus to the apex of the head of the fibula.
Function
Part of the posterolateral corner of the knee. It resists external rotation of the tibia on the femur.
